summary: The program's momentum gravity is the massive spin-2 field X. Between two ordinary bodies the record gives it as a Yukawa term added to Newton's potential. The term has gravitational strength (α = 4/3 in the aligned vacuum, u = 1) and a range below 37.7 μm. No document gives it any velocity dependence. The dependence derived here is only the spin-2 tensor factor: (3γ²−1)/2 ≈ 1 + (3/2)v²/c² for X, against 2γ²−1 ≈ 1 + 2v²/c² for the graviton. Carried through to a two-body Lagrangian, the graviton case reproduces the EIH velocity terms exactly. The only relative-velocity gate in the program acts between conjugate-matter (χ) particles, through the momentum-fiber width of χ quanta. It multiplies a contact interaction about 10⁴⁰ times stronger than gravity at the benchmark. So between two χ bodies it is velocity-gated scattering where the bodies overlap, not a perturbation of the 1/r law, and their gravity stays ungated (equivalence principle). Between χ and ordinary matter the record gives only ordinary gravity; any X term is sub-millimetre and ungated, or absent at tree level under the Siegel-block reading. An interaction that depends only on momenta exerts no force (ṗ = 0), so the chat-only 'Yukawa in momentum', read as a potential, changes only how velocity relates to momentum. A velocity-gated perturbation of gravity therefore needs a 1/r potential multiplied by a gate, which is Paul's picture (model b). That model is Galilean invariant when the gate uses relative velocity, and it moves momentum only between near-co-moving bodies. It necessarily changes inertia at relative order 2β|Φ|/v*², and it turns orbits backward by about 4πβGM/(a v*²) per orbit, about 4×10⁶ β times GR's rate. The program as written cannot supply such a long-range part. X's mass is common to all sources, so the laboratory bound also limits X's range between χ particles, unless X's coupling to ordinary matter is made far weaker than gravity. That contradicts #8 §3 and #11 §7.5, or the aligned vacuum. Separately, a long-range force no stronger than G cannot also make dwarf-galaxy cores, which would need about 3×10³¹ G. If X carries the transfer factor, the record's own contact gate needs X heavier than about 10–200 keV, a range below about 10⁻¹¹ m. The clumping problem tested only the contact model, so the obituary stands for the program as written. A long-range gated force is a different, untested model that would need new structure.

claims.statement: Spin-2 tensor factor. For point masses with T_i^{μν} = m_i u_i^μ u_i^ν, T1·T2 − c T1T2 = m1m2(γ² − c), where γ = u1·u2, exactly and in any frame. Normalized to its static value it is 2γ² − 1 for a massless graviton (c = ½; this is the Chebyshev polynomial T₂(γ)). It is (3γ² − 1)/2 for a Fierz–Pauli field (c = ⅓; the Legendre polynomial P₂(γ)). Series: 1 + 2v² + 2v⁴ and 1 + (3/2)v² + (3/2)v⁴, with v in units of c. Relative-velocity dependence therefore first enters at O(v²/c²), and to that order it depends only on |v1 − v2|. The k k/M² terms of the Fierz–Pauli numerator drop on conserved point sources. Anchor: the γ → ∞ ratio of the two factors is 3/4, the vDVZ light-bending deficit.

claims.statement: From amplitude to two-body Lagrangian, compared with EIH. The procedure: V(q) = −amplitude/(4E1E2), retardation from 1/(q² − ω²) with ω² → (q·v1)(q·v2), and L_int = −V at first order. It reproduces the Darwin Lagrangian for spin 1. For the massless spin 2 it reproduces exactly the O(G) velocity terms of the EIH Lagrangian, (G m1m2/r)[1 + (3/2)(v1²+v2²) − (7/2)v1·v2 − ½(n·v1)(n·v2)]/c². The EIH form is from Will 2018, eq. (9), with GR values G = B = D = 1, A = C = E = 0 [S]. That transcription was checked: the EIH equations of motion derived from it match Wikipedia's EIH acceleration [S] to 1e-41 in 3 random configurations. For the massive spin-2 term at r ≪ λ_X the result is (αGm1m2/r)e^{−r/λ}[1 + (v1²+v2²) − (5/2)v1·v2 − ½(n·v1)(n·v2)]/c², plus a retardation piece −(M_X/2)(n·v1)(n·v2)e^{−r/λ}. In the CM frame, GR gives [(3+ν)v² + ν(n·v)²]/2 and the massive term gives (1 + ν/2)v² + ν(n·v)²/2: both functions of the relative velocity and its angle to n. In a general frame the EIH velocity terms are (3/2)|v1−v2|² − ½v1·v2 − ½(n·v1)(n·v2), which is not a function of v1 − v2 alone (1PN dynamics is Lorentz, not Galilean, invariant [T]†). Sizes: (v/c)² = 1.1e-7 at 100 km/s and 1.0e-6 at 300 km/s.

claims.statement: Model (a): a potential depending only on momenta, H = Σp²/2m + U(argument). Hamilton's equations give ṗ_i = 0 exactly and ẋ_i = p_i/m_i + ∂U/∂p_i, an anomalous velocity. The interaction cannot change any momentum, so it cannot scatter, exert a force or clump the momentum distribution. It changes only the velocity–momentum relation: the inverse mass is shifted by ∂²U/∂p², which depends on the neighbours' momenta. Lagrangian to first order: L = Σ½m v² − U(m1v1 − m2v2) + O(U²). Galilean invariance requires the reduced-mass relative momentum k = (m2p1 − m1p2)/M, or p1/m1 − p2/m2. With p1 − p2 the boost shift is (m1 − m2)u, and d(m1x1 + m2x2)/dt − P = (m1 − m2)∇U ≠ 0. The literal Born image of p²/2m + V(x) is x²/2m + V(p), with ẋ = V′(p) and ṗ = −x/m: the swap also turns the kinetic term into a harmonic trap.

claims.statement: Structural consequence. Any interaction that transfers momentum must depend on positions, since ṗ_i = −∂H/∂x_i. A gate in relative velocity can only switch a position-dependent interaction on or off: model (b) for a 1/r force, model (c) for a contact force. The lab notebook's founding mean field, ε(p; f) = p²/2m + ∫U(p − p′)f̄(p′), cannot change the momentum distribution at all wherever f̄ is uniform in x. Exchanging the roles of x and v in the Jeans problem would also turn the kinetic term into x²/2m, which χ does not have (#11 §8: χ has ordinary kinematics on g). Calc note #2's version is local in x (contact), which is what lets its mean field move momenta.

claims.statement: Model (b), algebra: L = Σ½m v² + G̃ m1m2 W(|v1−v2|/v*)/r with W(0) = 1, which is Paul's long-range force gated in relative velocity. The canonical momentum p_i ≠ m_i v_i, and the conserved energy is Σ½mv² − (G̃m1m2/r)[W − wW′]. The Lagrangian is Galilean invariant up to a total derivative. The first-order Hamiltonian is H = Σp²/2m − G̃m1m2 W(|p1/m1 − p2/m2|/v*)/r. Hamilton's equations: ṗ1 = −G̃m1m2 W (x1 − x2)/r³, the Newtonian force times the gate, and ẋ1 = p1/m1 − (G̃m1m2/r)∂W/∂p1. With a Gaussian W the relative-motion Hessian of the Lagrangian at v_rel = 0 is μ(1 − 2G̃M/(r v*²)), so the effective inertia vanishes at r* = 2G̃M/v*². This is a Helmholtz-type objection, as raised against Weber's velocity-dependent force †. In Hamiltonian form the inverse inertia is (1/μ)(1 + 2G̃M/(r v*²)), the same at first order. The relative inertia change is therefore 2β|Φ|/v*² for G̃ = βG. The gate argument |p1/m1 − p2/m2| conserves the centre-of-mass motion; |p1 − p2|/(m1v*) does not.
claims.basis: Symbolic 3D Lagrangian with generic W: energy function, boost, Hessian, first-order Legendre check, Hamilton's equations, CM check.

claims.statement: Model (b), two-body numerics. The relative-coordinate Hamiltonian p²/2 − (1 + βe^{−p²})/r is regular gravity plus a gated perturbation of strength β (units GM = μ = v* = 1, planar). Bound orbits turn backward (retrograde precession). At leading order the shift is Δω = −4πβGM/(a v*²(1 − e²)) per orbit, against GR's +6πGM/(ac²(1−e²)): per unit β, (−4/6)(c/v*)² = −4.2×10⁶ times GR's rate at v* = 120 km/s. Numerics confirm the formula as GM/(av*²) → 0 (measured/formula 0.987 at 1/300, 0.963 at 1/100). For GM/(av*²) ≳ 0.1 the shift saturates, at about 0.2–0.3 rad per orbit for β = 0.2. Flybys (β = 0.5, b = 20GM/v*²): at v∞ ≫ v* the deflection tends to the Rutherford value for G (0.011112 vs 0.011111 at v∞ = 3v*). At v∞ ≲ v* it is enhanced in shallow encounters. In deep ones, where gravity itself speeds the pair past v*, the gate closes near pericentre and the anomalous velocity changes the orbit at O(1). At v∞ = 0.1v* the deflection is 2.32 rad, below even Rutherford for G (2.75). The integrator reproduces Rutherford at β = 0 and is unchanged under step halving. Energy and angular momentum are conserved to 10⁻¹³ and 10⁻¹⁴.

claims.statement: Model (c), the gated contact interaction of calc note #2, smoothed with width ε: U = −g δ_ε(x1 − x2) G((p1 − p2)/μ). Hamilton's equations give ṗ1 = g·G·∇δ_ε and ẋ1 = p1/m − g δ_ε ∂G/∂p1. Both act only while the bodies overlap: the force gradient at r = 10ε is 3×10⁻²¹ of its maximum, and deflections at b = 10 are ~10⁻²¹ rad. Its effect on velocities is through collisions, i.e. SIDM with a gated σ_T. Collective motion appears only if g n_gate ≥ m min(σ, v*)², a criterion missed by 28–31 orders at the benchmark (record). The p1 − p2 argument is Galilean invariant only for equal masses, which covers χχ. Between separated bodies it exerts no force.

claims.statement: Galilean invariance of gate arguments. Relative velocity v_i − v_j (or p_i/m_i − p_j/m_j) and the reduced-mass relative momentum k = μ(v_i − v_j) are invariant. The momentum difference p_i − p_j shifts by (m_i − m_j)u under a boost, so it is invariant only for equal masses. A non-invariant gate implies a preferred frame. The coupling between unequal bodies would then depend on their common velocity relative to that frame, and the centre of mass of an isolated pair would not move uniformly (d(Σm x)/dt ≠ P), while canonical momentum is still conserved. The program's χχ gate is invariant: #11 §8 uses k, and #6 §4's p1 − p2 equals 2k for equal masses. Any gate between bodies of different mass, such as χ–SM pairs or composites, must use k.

claims.statement: Inertia, and #13's dual inertia. Models (a) and (b) inevitably modify ordinary inertia. In (b) the relative change is ε = 2β|Φ|/v*², with v* = 120 km/s: ε/β is 0.12 for Earth's orbit (if ordinary matter were gated) and 7.3 for the MW potential at the Sun. For a χ particle in the MW halo, gated only by its co-moving fraction n_gate/n = 0.029, it is 0.22. It is 0.04 in a classical dwarf and 0.006 in an ultra-faint dwarf. GR's analogous terms are of order |Φ|/c², about 10⁻⁶. #13 §5's dual inertia is a different thing: λ_χ as resistance to force change, with constant-force states as dual-inertial (conjecture-tier). It would need the Born-swapped kinetic term x²/2m̃, which gives ṗ = −x/m̃. None of (a)–(c) has that term, and #11 §8 gives χ ordinary kinematics.

claims.statement: Forcing chain and how far the range bound reaches. #11 §7.1 and #6 §1–§3: shift symmetry makes X never auxiliary, dual diffeomorphisms make it a second graviton, the multi-graviton no-go [8†] excludes massless X, and Higgsing of dual diffeomorphisms gives M_X = the polarization-breaking scale. The chain forces M_X > 0 but sets no scale, and the record gives M_X no value, so the chain alone does not forbid a light X (M_X c² = 6.4×10⁻²⁷ eV for a 1 kpc range). M_X is a property of the field, so λ_X is the same for every source. At fixed ordinary-matter coupling α = (4/3)u², the bound λ_X < 37.7 μm therefore limits X's range between χ particles too. What differs by source is only the strength, since χ's dual-stress coupling is separate. The bound moves only by weakening X's coupling to ordinary matter (57.0 μm at u = 0.5), or by screening.

claims.statement: Routes to a kpc-range part, and what each contradicts. (1) A non-aligned vacuum (u ≪ 1). Its vacuum energy is of order the spin-2 mass squared (diameter note §8.2), (M_X/H0)² = 2×10¹³ for a 1 kpc range. That is acceptable only if λ_X ≳ c/H0 = 4.45 Gpc. It gives up the aligned-point vacuum-energy identity (#11 §7.3), and unscreened Cassini still needs u < 6×10⁻³. (2) M_f ≠ M_g contradicts #8 §3's reciprocity argument. (3) Decoupling ordinary matter from X at linear order, as in the Siegel reading of P5, contradicts #11 §7.5 and #8 §3 as written. (4) Vainshtein screening. For λ_X = 1 kpc the Sun's r_V ≈ 1.2×10³ AU, so the inner Solar System could be screened †. A galaxy with 10¹⁰ M_⊙ inside 1 kpc has r_V ≈ 12 pc, so galactic scales stay unscreened. There lensing and dynamics would differ, with γ = 5/7 at u = 1, the kind of test in Enander and Mörtsell 2013, which the diameter note cites [S]. The massive term would also make G inside λ_X differ from G beyond it. (5) A light dark mediator φ for the transfer factor 1/(q² + m_φ²). It contradicts the benchmark m_φ ~ m_χ (#1 §5.1) and row 2's isotropy if it is also the SIDM mediator. Otherwise it is a new, underived postulate; P4 strict forbids it to couple to SM, and it would make χ and stars fall differently in a χ halo's field (dark-sector equivalence-principle violation). (6) A light massive spin-2 is strongly coupled below 1/Λ3 ≈ 43 m for a kpc range †. None of the routes gives a gated force between ordinary bodies, since the record gives SM quanta no fiber width.

claims.statement: Strength mismatch: one interaction cannot be both the SIDM gate and a long-range perturbation of gravity. A long-range χχ force that made dwarf-galaxy cores by scattering (σ0 = 3.7×10⁻²⁴ cm² at 30 km/s, screened-Coulomb σ_T) needs strength A ≈ 1.1×10⁻⁹, which is 3.3×10³¹ G m_χ². That would be catastrophic for halos. Conversely, X at gravitational strength (α = 4/3) with a 37.7 μm range gives σ_T/σ0 = 2×10⁻⁶³. So the record's single X cannot both make σ0 and act at long range: the dual-stress enhancement OP5 would have to switch off at long range. A long-range gated component would have to be a separate, weak (≲ G) interaction that does not make cores.

claims.statement: Paul's literal question, answered for each reading. (R1) X between ordinary bodies, as recorded: an extra attraction on top of Newtonian gravity, of gravitational strength, but confined below 37.7 μm. Its dependence on relative velocity is only the spin-2 factor (3γ²−1)/2 ≈ 1 + (3/2)v²/c², about 10⁻⁷ at 100 km/s, with no gate. Not a velocity-dependent perturbation at astronomical distances. (R2) The record's χχ interaction: strongly dependent on relative velocity (gated at v* ~ 100 km/s), but it is a contact interaction of strength about 10⁴⁰ G, not a perturbation of the 1/r law. Two χ bodies feel it only where they overlap, as gated scattering; their gravity is ungated. (R3) χ with an ordinary body: no. Ordinary gravity only; any X term is sub-38 μm and ungated, or absent at tree level. (R4) GR itself: yes, mildly. In the CM frame the EIH terms are a relative-velocity-dependent correction of relative size [(3+ν)v² + ν(n·v)²]/(2c²), about 10⁻⁷ at 100 km/s, growing with speed and not gated. (R5) The chat-only 'Yukawa in momentum' read as a momentum-space potential: no. It exerts no force (ṗ = 0) and only changes how velocity follows momentum. (R6) Paul's long-range gated model: yes by construction, but it is not in the program as written. It needs a light carrier coupled to χ that cannot also make dwarf cores. It changes inertia at relative order 2β|Φ|/v*² and precesses orbits at (c/v*)² ≈ 4×10⁶ times GR's rate per unit β. Acting on ordinary matter it is excluded unless β ≲ 10⁻⁷.

The obituary's reach. The clumping problem tested a contact interaction gated in momentum: calc note #2 'the x-range collapsed to contact', and calc note #3 a gated contact attraction. Its particle-island shortfall of 10²⁸–10³¹ uses a coupling g fixed by σ0. For the program as written there is no long-range gated component, so the obituary stands. A long-range gated force (model b) is a different model that the clumping problem never evaluated. Its mean field carries the long-range kernel ∝ 1/k², so its stability threshold is Jeans-like, not calc note #2's criterion. Its strength would be ≲ G, not set by σ0 (P19). Whether it clumps, and whether it survives other constraints, is outside this record.

open_questions: Does ordinary matter couple linearly to X? The record gives two pictures. In the Siegel parametrization X enters the position block of H_Z only at second order. In the bimetric frame picture, #8 §3 and #11 §7.5 give gravitational strength. The answer decides whether the torsion-balance bound applies to X at all (related: flag 39).
Is the transfer factor 1/(q² + m_φ²) carried by X (m_φ = M_X) or by a separate dark mediator? If by X, the record's contact gate and row 2's isotropy need M_X ≳ 10–200 keV (λ_X ≲ 10⁻¹¹ m).

Does the fiber-overlap gate act on graviton exchange between χ quanta? The record says χ gravity is ungated (χ propagates on g; equivalence principle) but derives no reason why only the dual-stress coupling sees the fiber width.

What is the mean-field stability threshold of a long-range attraction gated in relative velocity (model b) for χ in halos? Its kernel ∝ 1/k² makes it Jeans-like, not calc note #2's contact criterion. Not evaluated here (clumping task).
Could the program supply a light, dark-only mediator with strength ≲ G? No document derives one, and P4 strict forbids it to couple to ordinary matter.
